A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research, despite the revised title and HAPO-to-APO renaming. Their complete main texts, appendices, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original RoboMimic and real-robot experiments, including success rates, lifelong-learning outcomes and failure-recovery examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original simulation and real-robot results in Tables 1–7, lifelong-learning results in Figure 4, and qualitative recovery examples in Figure 6.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 retains the same warm start, intervention labeling, deployment–optimization loop, balanced sampling and adaptive preference weighting. The objectives and π0-FAST decoding fallback are unchanged; renaming HAPO to APO does not change the method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same four RoboMimic tasks, position/background/texture disruptions, and real-world insertion, cup-hanging and lemon-placement tasks. The additional main-text mentions in v3 describe experiments already present in v1's appendix.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain the base policy, Dagger, Sirius, DPO, TPO and KTO. The π0-FAST and real-world comparisons retain the base policy, Dagger and TPO. No comparator is added or removed within corresponding experiments.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, training settings, demonstration and interaction counts, disruption-adaptation procedure, and evaluation trial counts remain unchanged. Moving appendix evidence into the main text introduces no new evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: The recovery case study moves from v1 Appendix C to v3 Section 4.7, but Figure 6 shrinks from five examples to three. Background-disrupted real-world insertion and simulated square-insertion recovery examples are removed. The disruption, retention and lifelong-learning analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both report the same simulation evaluation under three unseen seeds and average success rates. There are no changes to reported run counts, uncertainty estimation, error bars, confidence intervals or significance testing.

E6.justification: All tabulated scores and lifelong-learning curves are unchanged. The 85%, 85%, 90% and 95% Insert Square column added to v3 Table 4 repeats v1 Table 6, which v3 also retains. The substantive result removal is limited to the two qualitative recovery examples omitted from Figure 6.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same reward ratio, utility, KL term, loss and adaptive-weight definitions. No assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs are added, removed or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The revised title, abstract and introduction emphasize post-deployment refinement, but retain the same scientific claims: human-assisted action preferences and adaptive reweighting support failure correction, stable continual improvement and robust VLA adaptation.

C2.justification: The explanations of knowledge retention, adaptive weighting and learned failure recovery remain substantively unchanged. The autoregressive-only limitation is retained under the renamed Discussion and Future Work paragraph; the recovery interpretation is relocated from the appendix.

D1.justification: v3 adds an explicit code-repository link on its first page, whereas v1 provides only a project-page link. Hardware, hyperparameters, KL estimation, gripper-token handling and the π0-FAST decoding fallback were already documented in v1.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations on dynamic-movement-primitive robot skills, KOI online imitation learning, and embodied learning for object-centric manipulation. The existing positioning relative to DPO, KTO, Grape and human-in-the-loop learning remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper, renames HAPO to APO, and revises the abstract and portions of the introduction and conclusion. It promotes appendix recovery discussion to Section 4.7 and relabels subsequent appendix sections, while retaining the overall organization and most technical prose.

P2.justification: v3 duplicates the intervention illustration in the main text, relocates and reduces the recovery montage, and adds previously reported real-world scores as a Table 4 column. It also fixes the overlapping figure/table captions on page 9. The overall visual format remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves accessibility through explicit code-access information, clearer caption spacing on page 9, and greater main-text visibility of existing recovery and real-world evidence. Quantitative support is unchanged, and removing two recovery examples slightly reduces qualitative breadth. The net benefit is limited to presentation and access rather than stronger scientific validation.
